answer: Retrospective Kernel Audit. Each action carries an identity-specific kernel derived from its registration fingerprint; the system clusters identities whose kernel overlap exceeds chance. A flag needs a pigment match across three independent behavioral traces, not one. To sustain N fake identities, an attacker must pay per-identity copper: a distinct registration artifact, then keep each kernel statistically separable from the cluster for the audit window. Costs scale linearly per identity, and evasion requires deliberate divergence that raises per-identity effort.
